name: CI

on:
  workflow_call:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  test:
    name: Typecheck, test and build
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd # v6.0.2
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up pnpm
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@fc06bc1257f339d1d5d8b3a19a8cae5388b55320 # v4.4.0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@48b55a011bda9f5d6aeb4c2d9c7362e8dae4041e # v6.4.0
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Typecheck
        run: pnpm typecheck

      - name: Test
        run: pnpm test

      - name: Build
        run: pnpm build

name: Publish image

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: publish-image-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  AWS_REGION: us-east-1
  IMAGE_REPOSITORY: 795637471508.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/posthog-depot-mcp

jobs:
  quality-gate:
    name: Exact-commit quality gate
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml
    permissions:
      contents: read

  publish:
    name: Build and push OCI image
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    needs: quality-gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd # v6.0.2
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@8df5847569e6427dd6c4fb1cf565c83acfa8afa7 # v6.0.0
        with:
          role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::795637471508:role/github-depot-mcp-publish-role
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Log in to Amazon ECR
        uses: aws-actions/amazon-ecr-login@062b18b96a7aff071d4dc91bc00c4c1a7945b076 # v2.0.1

      - name: Image metadata and ordered release tag
        id: meta
        uses: ./.github/actions/container-image-metadata
        with:
          images: ${{ env.IMAGE_REPOSITORY }}
          generate-ordered-release-tag: "true"

      # The runner is arm64. QEMU builds the amd64 variant.
      - name: Set up QEMU
        uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@99012661954931238ded8c8b007157a8430204e1 # v4.4.0

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@4d04d5d9486b7bd6fa91e7baf45bbb4f8b9deedd # v4.0.0

      - name: Build and push
        id: build
        uses: docker/build-push-action@ca052bb54ab0790a636c9b5f226502c73d547a25 # v5.4.0
        with:
          context: .
          push: true
          provenance: false
          platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
          annotations: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.annotations }}
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max

      - name: Publish ordered release alias
        uses: ./.github/actions/container-image-metadata
        with:
          images: ${{ env.IMAGE_REPOSITORY }}
          publish-ordered-release-tag: "true"
          ordered-release-tag: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.ordered-release-tag }}
          ordered-release-digest: ${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}

# Vendored from PostHog/shared-actions container-image-metadata at
# 2427cf9968667894226f164eab356d96ca930b22 (shared-actions#51). That repository is
# internal, and GitHub does not let a public repository use its actions. Keep this
# copy in step with that commit: Kargo freight discovery reads these tags and
# annotations.

name: "container image metadata"
description: >-
  Tags, labels and OCI provenance annotations for a service container build --
  the deploy-pipeline contract consumed by Kargo (PostHog/charts#12696). Wraps
  docker/metadata-action so every service stamps identical provenance: the
  standard org.opencontainers.image.* set plus commit author, committer,
  subject and committer timestamp, emitted as INDEX-LEVEL OCI annotations.
  Index-level matters: Kargo's freight discovery reads only OCI annotations
  (image config labels are invisible to it), and without a platform constraint
  it surfaces only the index level. Kargo warehouses additionally key their
  commit-order freight gate on org.opencontainers.image.revision, so the
  annotation set here is a contract -- do not rename keys without checking the
  warehouse criteria expressions and deploy_info consumers in PostHog/charts.
  Run after actions/checkout (commit metadata falls back to git when the
  triggering event carries no head_commit). Feed all three outputs to
  docker/build-push-action: tags, labels, and annotations. Ordered release
  generation and publication require GNU coreutils `timeout`, as provided by
  Ubuntu GitHub-hosted runners.

inputs:
  images:
    required: true
    description: >-
      In the metadata phase, image repositories passed through unchanged to
      docker/metadata-action. In the publication phase, exactly one image
      repository (registry/name) is required, e.g.
      795637471508.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/posthog-myservice; missing,
      malformed, or multi-image values fail input validation.
  extra-tags:
    required: false
    description: >-
      Additional docker/metadata-action tag specs, one per line, APPENDED to
      the fixed contract tag (an immutable sha-<gitsha> tag — what Kargo
      image warehouses subscribe to). Deliberately additive rather than a
      replaceable tags input: a full-replace override would let a consumer
      silently drop the load-bearing sha- tag. No latest tag by default —
      re-pushing it fails on immutable ECR repos and nothing in the deploy
      pipeline reads it; consumers that want one pass
      "type=raw,value=latest,enable={{is_default_branch}}" here.
    default: ""
  generate-ordered-release-tag:
    required: false
    description: >-
      Compute the source-ordered release tag for an eligible default-branch
      build without adding it to the standard metadata tags. Generation is
      ignored when publish-ordered-release-tag is 'true'; the phases use
      separate action invocations. Generation runs only for push and manual
      dispatch events on the default branch. All other events and refs,
      including schedules, are excluded by an explicit step condition and
      produce no ordered-release annotation; failures within the allowed set
      remain fail-soft warnings. On a shallow checkout, the bounded
      --filter=tree:0 unshallow fetch registers origin as a promisor remote and
      marks the checkout as a partial clone. That mutation is ephemeral on
      GitHub-hosted runners but persists in self-hosted or reused checkouts.
    default: "false"
  publish-ordered-release-tag:
    required: false
    description: >-
      Run the bounded post-build publication and registry read-back phase.
      Invoke the action again after the required image build with this enabled;
      publication takes precedence when generation is also enabled because the
      phases use separate action invocations. Publication runs only for push
      and manual dispatch events on the default branch. All other events and
      refs, including schedules, are excluded by an explicit step condition
      and produce no ordered-release annotation; active publication retains
      its result annotations. The cross-invocation latency budget is at most
      355 seconds: 120 seconds for history fetch, 35 seconds for publication,
      and 20 seconds for each of up to six read-backs, plus a 10-second kill
      grace per command.
    default: "false"
  ordered-release-tag:
    required: false
    description: >-
      Source-ordered release tag returned by the pre-build invocation.
    default: ""
  ordered-release-digest:
    required: false
    description: >-
      Exact sha256 digest returned by the required image build. Index and
      single-manifest sources are both supported and retain this digest.
    default: ""

outputs:
  tags:
    description: "Image tags, for docker/build-push-action `tags`."
    value: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
  labels:
    description: "OCI labels, for docker/build-push-action `labels`."
    value: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
  annotations:
    description: >-
      Index-level OCI annotations (provenance contract), for
      docker/build-push-action `annotations`.
    value: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.annotations }}
  commit-subject:
    description: >-
      First line of the commit message, hard-capped at 160 chars (also
      annotated on the image).
    value: ${{ steps.commit.outputs.subject }}
  commit-timestamp:
    description: "Committer timestamp, ISO 8601 UTC (also annotated on the image)."
    value: ${{ steps.commit.outputs.iso }}
  commit-author:
    description: "Commit author (GitHub login on push events, git author name otherwise; also annotated on the image)."
    value: ${{ steps.commit.outputs.author }}
  commit-committer:
    description: "Committer (GitHub login on push events, git committer name otherwise; also annotated on the image)."
    value: ${{ steps.commit.outputs.committer }}
  ordered-release-tag:
    description: >-
      Source-ordered release tag, or empty when generation is disabled or
      unavailable.
    value: ${{ steps.ordered-release.outputs.tag }}
  ordered-release-result:
    description: >-
      Post-build reconciliation result, or empty when the ordered publication
      phase did not run.
    value: ${{ steps.ordered-release-publication.outputs.result }}

runs:
  using: "composite"
  steps:
    # Commit metadata with fallbacks: push events carry head_commit (whose
    # author/committer usernames are GitHub logins, matching what the charts
    # deploy_info historically records); other triggers fall back to git
    # name fields. The message can be multiline and annotations are one per
    # line, so only the subject line rides on the image — and the subject is
    # additionally HARD-CAPPED at 160 chars. Nothing bounds a single line
    # (PR titles alone reach 256 chars), and an unbounded value would flow
    # into every downstream consumer: the freight annotations, the
    # deployments-file deploy_info, promotion commit messages and
    # notifications. The legacy repository_dispatch path has already been
    # bitten by oversized commit messages (client_payload caps at 64KB);
    # this contract bounds the value at the source instead. The committer
    # timestamp is forced to UTC so consumers never parse mixed offsets.
    - name: Extract commit metadata
      id: commit
      shell: bash
      env:
        COMMIT_MESSAGE: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        EVENT_AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.head_commit.author.username }}
        EVENT_COMMITTER: ${{ github.event.head_commit.committer.username }}
        # ${subject:0:157} and ${#subject} slice BYTES under a POSIX/C
        # locale, which can cut a multibyte character in half and stamp
        # invalid UTF-8 into the annotation. Pin the locale so slicing is
        # character-based regardless of the runner image's defaults.
        LC_ALL: C.UTF-8
      run: |
        # GITHUB_OUTPUT key injection (a value smuggling "\nkey=val") is
        # structurally prevented here, not by quoting: subject is truncated
        # to one line by head -n1, git rejects commit objects with newlines
        # in author/committer names, and GitHub logins cannot contain
        # newlines. Keep those properties in mind before swapping any of
        # these sources.
        subject="$(printf '%s' "${COMMIT_MESSAGE}" | head -n 1)"
        if [ -z "${subject}" ]; then
          subject="$(git log -1 --format=%s)"
        fi
        if [ "${#subject}" -gt 160 ]; then
          subject="${subject:0:157}..."
        fi
        author="${EVENT_AUTHOR:-$(git log -1 --format=%an)}"
        committer="${EVENT_COMMITTER:-$(git log -1 --format=%cn)}"
        {
          echo "subject=${subject}"
          echo "author=${author}"
          echo "committer=${committer}"
          echo "iso=$(TZ=UTC git show -s --date=format-local:%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ --format=%cd HEAD)"
        } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

    - name: Compute ordered release tag
      id: ordered-release
      if: (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') && inputs.publish-ordered-release-tag != 'true' && inputs.generate-ordered-release-tag == 'true' && github.ref == format('refs/heads/{0}', github.event.repository.default_branch)
      continue-on-error: true
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail

        skip_ordered_release_tag() {
          printf '::warning::Skipping ordered release tag because %s\n' "$1"
          printf 'tag=\n' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          exit 0
        }

        timeout_is_usable() {
          local version
          command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
          version="$(timeout --version 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
          [[ "$version" == *"GNU coreutils"* ]]
        }

        if ! shallow="$(git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository 2>/dev/null)"; then
          skip_ordered_release_tag "repository history could not be inspected"
        fi

        if [ "$shallow" = "true" ]; then
          if ! timeout_is_usable; then
            skip_ordered_release_tag "the GNU coreutils timeout prerequisite is unavailable"
          fi
          if ! timeout --kill-after=10s 120s git fetch \
            --no-tags \
            --prune \
            --no-recurse-submodules \
            --unshallow \
            --filter=tree:0 \
            origin \
            "+${GITHUB_REF}:refs/remotes/origin/${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"; then
            skip_ordered_release_tag "complete source history could not be fetched"
          fi
        fi

        if [ "$(git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository 2>/dev/null)" != "false" ]; then
          skip_ordered_release_tag "complete source history is unavailable"
        fi

        if ! head_revision="$(git rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null)" || [ "$head_revision" != "$GITHUB_SHA" ]; then
          skip_ordered_release_tag "the checked-out revision does not match GITHUB_SHA"
        fi

        if ! position="$(git rev-list --first-parent --count "$GITHUB_SHA" 2>/dev/null)"; then
          skip_ordered_release_tag "the source position could not be computed"
        fi

        case "$position" in
          ""|0|0*|*[!0-9]*)
            skip_ordered_release_tag "the source position is outside the supported range"
            ;;
        esac

        if [ "${#position}" -gt 12 ] || ! [[ "$GITHUB_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{6,}$ ]]; then
          skip_ordered_release_tag "the source position is outside the supported range"
        fi

        if ! printf -v tag 'r%012d-%.6s' "$position" "$GITHUB_SHA" ||
          ! [[ "$tag" =~ ^r[0-9]{12}-[0-9a-f]{6}$ ]]; then
          skip_ordered_release_tag "the source position is outside the supported range"
        fi

        printf 'tag=%s\n' "$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

    # DOCKER_METADATA_ANNOTATIONS_LEVELS=index is load-bearing, not a
    # preference: without it metadata-action emits labels only, which Kargo
    # cannot see; and index is the only level Kargo surfaces for a
    # multi-arch image without a platform constraint. Index-level
    # annotations also require the pushed artifact to be an OCI image index
    # -- multi-platform builds with buildkit's default provenance
    # attestations already produce one.
    - name: Docker meta
      id: meta
      uses: docker/metadata-action@030e881283bb7a6894de51c315a6bfe6a94e05cf # v6.0.0
      env:
        DOCKER_METADATA_ANNOTATIONS_LEVELS: index
      with:
        images: ${{ inputs.images }}
        # Fixed contract tag first; extra-tags are appended, never replace
        # (metadata-action ignores blank lines when extra-tags is empty).
        # The sha- prefix is part of the contract: Kargo warehouses filter
        # on ^sha-, and a prefixed tag stays self-describing next to pr-*,
        # semver, and branch tags in the same repo.
        tags: |
          type=sha,prefix=sha-,format=long
          ${{ inputs.extra-tags }}
        annotations: |
          com.posthog.image.author=${{ steps.commit.outputs.author }}
          com.posthog.image.committer=${{ steps.commit.outputs.committer }}
          com.posthog.image.message=${{ steps.commit.outputs.subject }}
          com.posthog.image.commit-timestamp=${{ steps.commit.outputs.iso }}

    - name: Validate ordered release publication inputs
      id: ordered-release-validation
      if: (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') && inputs.publish-ordered-release-tag == 'true' && github.ref == format('refs/heads/{0}', github.event.repository.default_branch)
      shell: bash
      env:
        ORDERED_RELEASE_IMAGE: ${{ inputs.images }}
        ORDERED_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ inputs.ordered-release-tag }}
        ORDERED_RELEASE_DIGEST: ${{ inputs.ordered-release-digest }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail

        fail_input() {
          printf '::error title=Invalid ordered image alias input::%s\n' "$1" >&2
          exit 2
        }

        repository="${ORDERED_RELEASE_IMAGE:-}"
        ordered_tag="${ORDERED_RELEASE_TAG:-}"
        expected_digest="${ORDERED_RELEASE_DIGEST:-}"
        source_revision="${GITHUB_SHA:-}"

        if [ -z "$ordered_tag" ]; then
          printf '%s\n' '::notice::Skipping ordered image alias publication because no ordered tag was generated'
          printf 'skip=true\n' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          exit 0
        fi

        while [[ "$repository" == [[:space:]]* ]]; do
          repository="${repository:1}"
        done
        while [[ "$repository" == *[[:space:]] ]]; do
          repository="${repository:0:${#repository}-1}"
        done

        case "$repository" in
          ""|-*|*[[:space:]@,]*)
            fail_input "The publication phase requires exactly one image repository without whitespace, a digest, or a list separator"
            ;;
        esac

        registry="${repository%%/*}"
        repository_name="${repository#*/}"
        if [ "$registry" = "$repository" ]; then
          fail_input "The publication phase requires an image repository in registry/name form"
        fi
        case "$registry" in
          ""|-*|*[[:space:]@,]*)
            fail_input "The publication phase requires exactly one untagged image repository in registry/name form"
            ;;
        esac
        case "$repository_name" in
          ""|-*|*[[:space:]@,]*|*:*)
            fail_input "The publication phase requires exactly one untagged image repository in registry/name form"
            ;;
        esac
        if ! [[ "$registry" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9]+([.-][a-zA-Z0-9]+)*(:[0-9]+)?$ ]] ||
          ! [[ "$repository_name" =~ ^[a-z0-9]+(([._]|__|-+)[a-z0-9]+)*(/[a-z0-9]+(([._]|__|-+)[a-z0-9]+)*)*$ ]]; then
          fail_input "The publication phase image repository is malformed"
        fi

        if ! [[ "$ordered_tag" =~ ^r[0-9]{12}-[0-9a-f]{6}$ ]] ||
          ! [[ "$expected_digest" =~ ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] ||
          ! [[ "$source_revision" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{6,}$ ]] ||
          [ "${ordered_tag##*-}" != "${source_revision:0:6}" ]; then
          fail_input "The ordered tag, digest, and source revision must be present, valid, and revision-matched"
        fi

        printf 'image=%s\n' "$repository" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

    - name: Publish and reconcile ordered release tag
      id: ordered-release-publication
      if: (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') && inputs.publish-ordered-release-tag == 'true' && github.ref == format('refs/heads/{0}', github.event.repository.default_branch) && steps.ordered-release-validation.outputs.skip != 'true'
      continue-on-error: true
      shell: bash
      env:
        ORDERED_RELEASE_IMAGE: ${{ steps.ordered-release-validation.outputs.image }}
        ORDERED_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ inputs.ordered-release-tag }}
        ORDERED_RELEASE_DIGEST: ${{ inputs.ordered-release-digest }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail

        timeout_is_usable() {
          local version
          command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
          version="$(timeout --version 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
          [[ "$version" == *"GNU coreutils"* ]]
        }

        if ! timeout_is_usable; then
          printf '%s\n' '::error title=Ordered image alias read-back unavailable::GNU coreutils timeout is required for bounded ordered image alias publication and read-back' >&2
          printf 'result=unknown\n' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          exit 0
        fi

        # Keep the 20s read-back and 35s publication bounds in sync with the publish-ordered-release-tag latency budget above.
        inspect_digest() {
          local reference="$1"
          local output
          local status=0

          output="$(timeout --kill-after=10s 20s \
            docker buildx imagetools inspect \
            --format '{{json .Manifest.Digest}}' "$reference" 2>/dev/null)" || status=$?

          if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
            return "$status"
          fi

          if [[ "$output" =~ ^\"(sha256:[0-9a-f]{64})\"$ ]]; then
            printf '%s\n' "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
            return 0
          fi

          return 65
        }

        classify_alias() {
          local target="$1"
          local source="$2"
          local expected="$3"
          local observed

          if observed="$(inspect_digest "$target")" || observed="$(inspect_digest "$target")"; then
            if [ "$observed" = "$expected" ]; then
              printf '%s\n' present-at-expected-digest
            else
              printf '%s\n' integrity-mismatch
            fi
          elif inspect_digest "$source" >/dev/null; then
            printf '%s\n' absent
          else
            printf '%s\n' unknown
          fi
        }

        repository="$ORDERED_RELEASE_IMAGE"
        ordered_tag="$ORDERED_RELEASE_TAG"
        expected_digest="$ORDERED_RELEASE_DIGEST"
        target_image="${repository}:${ordered_tag}"
        source_image="${repository}@${expected_digest}"
        publication_status=0
        candidate=""
        observed=""
        if observed="$(inspect_digest "$target_image")"; then
          if [ "$observed" = "$expected_digest" ]; then
            candidate=present-at-expected-digest
          else
            candidate=integrity-mismatch
          fi
        elif ! inspect_digest "$source_image" >/dev/null && observed="$(inspect_digest "$target_image")"; then
          if [ "$observed" = "$expected_digest" ]; then
            candidate=present-at-expected-digest
          else
            candidate=integrity-mismatch
          fi
        fi
        if [ -z "$candidate" ]; then
          timeout --kill-after=10s 35s \
            docker buildx imagetools create --prefer-index=false --tag "$target_image" "$source_image" >&2 || publication_status=$?
          candidate="$(classify_alias "$target_image" "$source_image" "$expected_digest")" || candidate=unknown
        fi

        case "$candidate" in
          present-at-expected-digest)
            if [ "$publication_status" -eq 0 ]; then
              printf '%s\n' '::notice title=Ordered image alias present::Registry read-back confirmed the expected build digest' >&2
            else
              printf '::notice title=Ordered image alias present::Registry read-back confirmed the expected build digest after publication client status %s\n' "$publication_status" >&2
            fi
            ;;
          absent)
            printf '::warning title=Ordered image alias absent::Registry read-back confirmed absence after publication client status %s\n' "$publication_status" >&2
            ;;
          integrity-mismatch)
            printf '%s\n' '::error title=Ordered image alias integrity mismatch::Registry read-back returned a different digest' >&2
            ;;
          unknown)
            printf '%s\n' '::error title=Ordered image alias read-back unavailable::Registry read-back could not determine the ordered alias state' >&2
            ;;
          *)
            candidate=unknown
            printf '%s\n' '::error title=Ordered image alias read-back unavailable::Registry read-back could not determine the ordered alias state' >&2
            ;;
        esac
        printf 'result=%s\n' "$candidate" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

# depot-mcp

A small, read-only [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server for the [Depot](https://depot.dev) API.

Depot gives agents a CLI, but no MCP server. This server lets an agent read Depot CI failures, job logs, GitHub Actions jobs on Depot runners, and container builds. The agent does not need the `depot` CLI in its sandbox.

- **Transport:** Streamable HTTP, stateless. One endpoint: `POST /mcp`.
- **Auth:** Each request sends the caller's own Depot API token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The server sends that token to Depot and stores nothing.
- **Scope:** Read-only. No tool can start, cancel, retry or delete anything.

## Tools

### Depot CI

| Tool | Depot RPC | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ci_list_runs` | `CIService/ListRuns` | Find runs by repo, status, PR, SHA or trigger |
| `ci_get_run` | `CIService/GetRun` | Metadata and status of one run (no jobs or attempts) |
| `ci_list_workflows` | `CIService/ListWorkflows` | Find workflows |
| `ci_get_workflow` | `CIService/GetWorkflow` | A workflow with its jobs |
| `ci_diagnose_failure` | `CIService/GetFailureDiagnosis` | Why a run, workflow, job or attempt failed |
| `ci_get_job_summary` | `CIService/GetJobSummary` | Markdown job summary |
| `ci_get_job_logs` | `CIService/GetJobAttemptLogs` | Job attempt logs, with tail, step, stderr and text filters |
| `ci_list_artifacts` | `CIService/ListArtifacts` | Artifact metadata for a run |

### GitHub Actions on Depot runners

| Tool | Depot RPC | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gha_list_jobs` | `GithubActionsService/ListGithubActionsJobs` | Find jobs by repo, status, conclusion and time (default: last 24 hours) |
| `gha_get_job` | `GithubActionsService/GetGithubActionsJob` | One job |
| `gha_search_logs` | `GithubActionsService/SearchGithubActionsLogs` | Search log lines |
| `gha_get_log_context` | `GithubActionsService/GetGithubActionsLogContext` | Lines around a search match |
| `gha_list_job_runs` | `GithubActionsService/ListGithubActionsJobRuns` | Past runs of one job, to find flaky tests |
| `gha_get_test_results` | `GithubActionsService/GetGithubActionsTestResultsSummary` | Test results for a job |

### Container builds

| Tool | Depot RPC | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list_projects` | `core.v1.ProjectService/ListProjects` | Projects in the organization |
| `list_builds` | `core.v1.BuildService/ListBuilds` | Builds for a project |
| `get_build` | `core.v1.BuildService/GetBuild` | One build |
| `get_build_steps` | `build.v1.BuildService/GetBuildSteps` | Build steps, with errors |
| `get_build_step_logs` | `build.v1.BuildService/GetBuildStepLogs` | Logs for one build step |

Typical flow to debug a failed Depot CI run:

1. `ci_list_runs` with `status: ["failed"]`, `repo` and `pr`.
2. `ci_diagnose_failure` with `targetType: "run"` and the run ID.
3. `ci_get_job_logs` with an attempt ID from the diagnosis. Add `stderrOnly` or `contains` to make the output smaller.

`ci_get_run` does not return jobs or attempt IDs. Use `ci_diagnose_failure` or `ci_get_workflow` to get them.

`gha_list_jobs` uses a 24-hour window when you do not set `startAt` or `endAt`. Depot's own default is 30 days, and that can time out on large organizations.

## Known issues

- `gha_search_logs` returns `500 internal` from Depot. A direct call to `api.depot.dev` gives the same error, so the fault is in the Depot API. Because of this, `gha_get_log_context` is not tested: it needs a `lineId` from `gha_search_logs`.
- `get_build_step_logs` can return no lines, also for steps that ran for some seconds. The Depot API itself returns `{}` for these steps. Check `hasLogs` and `error` in `get_build_steps` first.

## Tokens

Use a Depot **organization token** (Organization settings → API tokens). Organization and user tokens can use every tool. Project tokens can use only the container build tools.

If you use a user token and belong to more than one organization, send `X-Depot-Org: <org-id>` as well.

## Run

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm start            # listens on PORT (default 3000)
```

Or with Docker:

```sh
docker build -t depot-mcp .
docker run -p 3000:3000 depot-mcp
```

Environment variables:

| Name | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PORT` | `3000` | HTTP port |
| `HOST` | `0.0.0.0` | Bind address |
| `DEPOT_API_URL` | `https://api.depot.dev` | Depot API base URL |
| `DEPOT_TIMEOUT_MS` | `60000` | Timeout for each Depot API call |

`GET /healthz` returns `{"status":"ok"}`.

Put the server behind TLS when you deploy it. The token goes in a request header.

## Connect a client

Claude Code:

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http depot https://<your-host>/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $DEPOT_TOKEN"
```

Any other MCP client that supports Streamable HTTP and custom headers works the same way.

## Development

```sh
pnpm dev          # run with reload
pnpm test         # vitest
pnpm typecheck
pnpm smoke PostHog/posthog   # call the tools on a running server with DEPOT_TOKEN from .env
```

The server calls Depot's Connect RPC API with plain JSON over `fetch`. Request field names come from Depot's protobuf definitions in [depot/proto](https://github.com/depot/proto) and [depot/cli](https://github.com/depot/cli/tree/main/proto/depot/ci/v1).

FROM node:22-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /app
RUN corepack enable
COPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml ./
RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
COPY tsconfig.json tsconfig.build.json ./
COPY src ./src
RUN pnpm build && pnpm prune --prod

FROM node:22-alpine
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production PORT=3000
COPY --from=build /app/package.json ./
COPY --from=build /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=build /app/dist ./dist
USER 1000:1000
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "dist/main.js"]
